items.title: Duffy Says an L3Harris Crew Was Working on the FAA Network When Flights Stopped. Its Stock Fell 4% After Hours
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said an L3Harris crew was switching FAA lines from copper wire to fiber when a router flooded the air traffic control network. L3Harris fell 4.2% after hours, and airlines owe stranded travelers nothing.

items.title: US to resume flights after air traffic network failure sparks chaos
items.summary: WASHINGTON, Nov 13 (Reuters) - The FAA lifted a nationwide ground stop on Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers caused chaos at US airports and triggered the longest shutdown since the September 11, 2001, attacks. items.title: FAA lifts ground stop flights, airline stocks fall
items.summary: Airline stocks fell right before Friday's close after the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop. Departing flights cannot take off, while flights already in the air may continue to their destination.

items.title: United, Other Airline Stocks Drop After Nationwide Flight Ground Stop. Rental Car Stocks Rise.
items.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the stoppage was due to “a communication issue impacting all Air Route Traffic Control Centers. FAA technicians are investigating the issue.”
